theorem: Let rho1 be PPT on A1 tensor B1 with dim(B1)<=3, and let rho2 be any bipartite state of Schmidt number <=k. Regroup rho1 tensor rho2 across (A1 A2):(B1 B2). If a composite Alice filter factors as K_A=L_A(K1 tensor I_A2) with rank(K1)<=2, and K_B is any composite Bob filter, every nonzero output has Schmidt number <=k. The result holds even when L_A and K_B act jointly across their two tensor factors. If rho2 is PPT, the output is PPT. The opposite-party and opposite-copy variants also hold. This is an elementary deduction from the known 2x2/2x3 PPT separability theorem, not a novelty claim.
proof: The unnormalized state sigma1=(K1 tensor I_B1)rho1(K1 tensor I_B1)^* is PPT with local support dimensions at most2 and3, hence separable by Horodecki et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9605038. Write sigma1=sum_j p_j [a_j tensor b_j], p_j>=0, and rho2=sum_m[t_m] with SR(t_m)<=k. After tensoring and regrouping, each pure vector (a_j tensor b_j) tensor t_m has Schmidt rank equal to SR(t_m)<=k. Thus sigma1 tensor rho2 has an explicit SR<=k positive decomposition, and arbitrary composite local maps L_A and K_B cannot increase the rank of any term. PPT preservation follows separately by local congruence.
kernel_slice_corollary: For Q tensor Q with Q the original 3x3 PPT/SN2 crosshatch state, any rank-four Alice map K:C^3 tensor C^3->C^4 whose kernel contains a full tensor slice v tensor C^3 or C^3 tensor v (v!=0) factors through a rank-two map on that factor. Hence every nonzero output after ANY Bob map has SN<=2; the same holds when Bob's kernel contains such a slice. For Q, the bound k=2 follows directly from its four rank2 defining kets and entanglement follows from its exact CES check in frontier-20261028-crosshatch-ces-source-check.py SHA256 0ed1abb9734c886ef3016bdc2e2b6c8e81afa47ddadceeb16a109b70258a5a88. The source Q tensor Q has SN4 by the explicit Chen–Yang–Tang import in frontier-20261028-crosshatch-sn4-coordinate-drop-v1.json SHA256 66821aab1e903d1b073ff09a5434366cd2e1d00dd4120c684dd6695d3cc7d8bf.
coordinate_count_and_properness: Of the 126 four-coordinate supports in a 3x3 local tensor grid, 45 use at most two first-factor rows and 45 use at most two second-factor columns; their intersection has 9 Cartesian 2x2 supports, so 81 are covered by this factor-slice argument. The separately verified frontier-20261028-crosshatch-one-side-coordinate-sn2-v1.json SHA256 63cf819098a373730645028bd9d0ee81ca515ef2b316ee922e60370e916ddf87 handles all126, including the remaining45. The present condition is not automatic: the rank-four coordinate selection {(0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,2)} touches all three rows and columns, so its kernel contains neither any v tensor C^3 nor any C^3 tensor v with v!=0. It is nonetheless covered by the separate exact coordinate result.
limits: The 2x3 PPT-separability theorem is a named external import, not re-proved here. The stated factor-slice condition is sufficient only; generic joint filters need not satisfy it. No arbitrary 4x4 PPT theorem, 2-block-positive target witness, novelty or external/formal review is claimed.
